Prevention: C. rotundus is difficult to control.
Seeds are considered as unimportant; tubers are the main means of spread
Clean tools and farm machinery after working in an infested area to prevent tubers being spread; especially important if the weed is not already present in the area
Do not accept potentially contaminated materials, e.g. soil on planting stock
Control established populations near waterways to prevent spread during flooding and storm events
Kill the weed prior to planting the crop by taking direct control action and applying glyphosate
Monitoring: Additional relevant crops: groundnut, sunflower, pulses, maize
Erect, perennial sedge (30-60 cm high), with extensive underground network composed of tubers.
Tubers dark brown/ black, irregular shaped, 1-2 cm long at maturity, with several buds.
Leaves linear with distinct midrib, 7 mm wide.
Inflorescence with several unequal 'branches', each 2-6 cm long, emerging from the tip of the stem; each with 3-8 purplish-brown flowerheads.
Inspect fields weekly, in particular during and shortly after the wet season, and consider direct control when the weed is found
Look for the weed in wetlands and along waterways.
Water and storm events can spread tubers so be particularly attentive after severe rain events
Direct Control: Tubers and rhizomes in the soil can be destroyed by dessication (most effective in dry soil) or exhausting food reserves.
Cultivate every 2-3 weeks until crop canopy forms: the weed is shade intolerant.
Tillage must be deep (>12cm) in order to disturb as many of the rhizomes as possible.
Place organic mulch (eg rice straw) over areas where the weed is expected to grow; this provides temporary suppression
If the soil is moist hand pulling is effective as the tubers are removed with the weed; remove the pulled weed from the field
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
RP) 400-600 cc/ ac (as a pre-planting measure) at suggested rate of 500cc/ac.
Glyphosate is extremely toxic to crops, so do not let the spray drift onto crops.
Do not cultivate or disturb the weeds for 10 days.
Winner 15 % EC) at a rate of 500cc/ac; apply 14 days after sowing.
